titel: Inheritance and gifting of securities portfolios
kurz: How the allowances renew every ten years, why the price on the date of death is decisive, and why without a power of attorney nobody can get at the securities account for months.

bloecke.md:
Every securities account changes owner at the latest when its holder dies. Unlike the price trend, this change can be planned decades in advance. Two taxes apply side by side. Inheritance and gift tax covers the transfer of the assets, the [[Flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer)|flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer)]] the price gains in the account. Neither tax is credited against the other.

The valuation date is decisive (Section 11 ErbStG, Inheritance and Gift Tax Act), that is, the date of death for an inheritance and the date of execution for a gift. Later developments no longer change the valuation. If the market falls by 30% four weeks after the date of death, the higher market value remains the tax base. The tax then falls due on assets that no longer exist at that level.

## Allowances and tax classes

bloecke.titel: Tax classes and personal allowances (Sections 15, 16 ErbStG)
kopf: Relationship to the deceased or donor

bloecke.md:
The tax class depends solely on the family relationship, not on income. It determines the allowance and the rate schedule. The differences are large. While a child pays no tax on an acquisition of €300,000, an unmarried partner is left with €280,000 taxable after deducting their allowance. At 30%, this results in €84,000 of tax.

In the event of inheritance, the pension allowance (Versorgungsfreibetrag) under Section 17 ErbStG is added to the personal allowance. It is €256,000 for the surviving spouse. For children, it is graded by age, from €52,000 (up to five years) to €10,300 (20 to 27 years). It is reduced by the capitalised value of survivors' pensions, so people insured in the statutory pension scheme are often left with little of it. For married couples living in a community of accrued gains (Zugewinngemeinschaft), Section 5 ErbStG also applies. Under it, the notional claim to equalisation of accrued gains remains tax-free, and it can reduce the taxable acquisition more than any allowance.

bloecke.titel: Tax rates by value band and tax class (Section 19 ErbStG)
bloecke.unter: The rate applies to the entire taxable acquisition, not just to the part above the threshold. This is why the tax jumps at the band thresholds.

bloecke.md:
## Valuation of a securities account on inheritance

Under Section 11(1) BewG (Valuation Act), listed securities are valued at the lowest price quoted on the regulated market on the valuation date. The closing price and the average price play no role. Units in investment funds are included at the redemption price under Section 11(4) BewG; according to the wording of the provision, this also applies to exchange-traded ETFs. Bank balances count at face value including accrued interest.

Property is valued under Sections 176 et seq. BewG. The sales comparison approach applies to individually owned flats and to one- and two-family houses, the income approach to residential rental properties and the cost approach to all other properties. Since the revision by the Annual Tax Act 2022 (Jahressteuergesetz), the property values (Grundbesitzwerte) determined in this way have been noticeably closer to market value than before. If the value is set too high, a lower fair market value (gemeiner Wert) can be proven by an expert report under Section 198 BewG. This is only worthwhile for larger deviations. In addition, under Section 13d ErbStG, 10% of the value of properties let for residential purposes is disregarded.

The father is widowed, and his daughter is the sole heir. On the date of death, the estate consists of a securities account worth €620,000 (lowest prices on the valuation date), bank balances of €40,000 and a let flat with a property value of €400,000.

- Flat at only 90% under Section 13d ErbStG: €360,000
- Total acquisition: €1,020,000
- Lump-sum allowance for inheritance costs (Erbfallkostenpauschbetrag, Section 10(5) no. 3 ErbStG): −€15,000
- Allowance for a child (Section 16 ErbStG): −€400,000
- Taxable acquisition: €605,000

Above €600,000, the class I tax rate rises from 15% to 19%, and it does so for the entire amount. Without hardship relief (Härteausgleich), that would be 605,000 × 19% = €114,950. Here, hardship relief under Section 19(3) ErbStG applies. For an acquisition of exactly €600,000, €90,000 would be due, and the additional tax may not exceed half of the excess amount of €5,000. The tax is therefore €92,500 instead of €114,950. The additional acquisition of €5,000 thus costs €2,500 in tax, not €24,950.

bloecke.titel: From estate to tax (illustrative calculation for the example above)
bloecke.unter: Almost the entire reduction in the taxable value comes from two deductions, the rental discount on the property and the personal allowance. The daughter herself keeps €967,500 of the estate after tax, because the rental discount, the lump-sum allowance and the personal allowance only reduce the taxable value.

bloecke.md: All gifts from the same person to the same person within ten years are added together (Section 14 ErbStG). The allowance therefore applies once per relationship and ten-year period, regardless of the number of transfers, and is then fully available again. If the donor starts transferring at 55, they can use it three times; if they start at 80, usually only once. Of the major planning options, this is the only one that costs nothing but time.

bloecke.titel: Four ways to transfer €1.2 million to a child (illustrative calculation, tax class I)
zeilen: three tranches, each ten years apart

bloecke.md:
The fourth row shows a second planning option. Each parent has their own allowance for each child. If the assets belong to only one parent, they can first be shared out between the spouses tax-free and then passed on by both. The drawback of staggering is the loss of control, because assets given away belong to the recipient. If the assets are still needed, usufruct, revocation clauses or legacies can be considered instead of an unconditional transfer.

## Usufruct

The usufructuary may use an item and keep its income, although they are no longer the owner (Section 1030 BGB, Civil Code). If the donor reserves the usufruct, its capitalised value reduces the value of the gift. Since 2009, this has happened immediately and in full; before that, the tax attributable to it was only deferred.

bloecke.erklaerung: Valuation of a lifelong usufruct under Section 14 BewG.
variablen: annual income to which the usufructuary is entitled; for property, the net rent after the costs they bear themselves
present value factor by age and sex; the BMF publishes the table for Section 14 BewG anew every year
the annual value may at most equal the value of the asset divided by 18.6 (Section 16 BewG)
bloecke.beispiel: A flat has a property value of €500,000 and an annual net rent of €18,000. The cap under Section 16 BewG is 500,000 ÷ 18.6 = €26,881. The €18,000 is below this and remains decisive. With a multiplier of around 11 for a 65-year-old donor, the capitalised value is €198,000. The gift is therefore only valued at €302,000 and stays below the child's allowance. The exact multiplier comes from the BMF table for the year in question. For valuation dates from 2026, at the age of 65 it is around 11.4 for men and around 12.6 for women.

bloecke.md: If the usufructuary dies considerably earlier than the life table assumes, the tax is corrected retrospectively to the recipient's disadvantage under Section 14(2) BewG, because the deduction was then too high. In addition, a property encumbered with usufruct is hard to sell and can hardly be used as security for a loan. The recipient does have ownership, but neither the rent nor free disposal. In such an arrangement, the waiver of the usufruct should be provided for from the outset, because such a waiver is itself another gift and triggers tax again.

## Family home

Section 13(1) nos. 4a to 4c ErbStG makes owner-occupied residential property tax-free, but under three different rules. Between spouses, a transfer during their lifetime is tax-free, with no limit on floor space, no holding period and no set-off against the allowance. If the spouse inherits, the house is also tax-free, but only if they move in without undue delay and live in it themselves for ten years. The same applies to children as heirs, additionally limited to 200 square metres of living space. The share above that is taxable in the normal way. The courts usually interpret “without undue delay” as six months. If the heir moves in later, the delay must be justified.

If the heir gives up owner occupation within the ten years, for example by selling, letting or moving, the exemption is lost retrospectively and in full. It is only retained for compelling reasons such as a need for long-term care or death. A change of job, a home that is too large or too small and a separation do not count. The exemption for the family home (Familienheim) therefore ties up your life planning for ten years. Set against this, in class I, is a tax of 11% to 19% of the property's value, depending on the value band.

## Access to the securities account

When the bank learns of the death, it blocks transactions until the heirs' status has been proven. A certificate of inheritance (Erbschein) is not strictly necessary for this. According to the case law of the Federal Court of Justice (BGH), an opened notarial will is sufficient, and banks may not demand a certificate of inheritance across the board (BGH, XI ZR 401/12). This saves fees and months. Overall, a notarial will is often cheaper than a certificate of inheritance applied for later.

It only goes faster with a power of attorney beyond death (Vollmacht über den Tod hinaus). It does not expire when the inheritance occurs. The authorised person can use it to manage holdings and pay ongoing costs while the succession is still unresolved. Just as important is the lasting power of attorney (Vorsorgevollmacht) in case someone becomes legally incapacitated during their lifetime. The emergency right of representation between spouses (Ehegattennotvertretungsrecht, Section 1358 BGB), in force since 2023, only covers health matters, is limited to six months and does not permit any transactions on an account or securities account.

Several heirs form a community of heirs (Erbengemeinschaft, Sections 2032 et seq. BGB). They can only dispose of estate assets jointly (Section 2040 BGB). A single heir therefore cannot sell a share, not even the part that is arithmetically attributable to them. In practice, the community of heirs is dissolved by transferring the positions to individual securities accounts. This happens without consideration and does not trigger flat-rate withholding tax.

bloecke.unter: The upper chain takes days, the lower one months. The difference is made by a power of attorney signed during the holder's lifetime.

bloecke.titel: Inheritance tax and flat-rate withholding tax
bloecke.md:
Inheritance tax is based on the full market value, without deducting the flat-rate withholding tax that arises on a later sale. At the same time, as universal successor (Gesamtrechtsnachfolger, Section 1922 BGB), the heir takes over the deceased's acquisition costs and acquisition date. For recipients of gifts, Section 20(4) sentence 6 EStG (Income Tax Act) expressly provides the same. The price on the date of death therefore does not become new acquisition costs.

In the example, the securities account is worth €620,000, and the deceased paid €300,000 for it. On sale, €320,000 of price gains must be taxed. At around 26.375%, that is roughly €84,400, in addition to the inheritance tax on the same value. Section 35b EStG provides for a reduction for income subject to double taxation, but it does not apply to capital income taxed at the flat rate. The deceased's loss offset pots do not pass to the heir either. The bank closes them as soon as it learns of the death and issues a loss certificate (BMF circular of 14 May 2025, para. 237). After that, the losses can only be offset in the deceased's income tax assessment for the year of death.

If spouses appoint each other as sole heirs and the children only as final heirs (Section 2269 BGB), the children's allowance in relation to the parent who dies first remains unused. With two children, that is €800,000. The same assets are also taxed twice, first for the surviving spouse and then for the children. Legacies to the children on the first death reduce this disadvantage.

schritte.text: It covers the case of legal incapacity during your lifetime. It should be notarially certified or notarised, because banks and the land registry often reject powers of attorney drawn up privately. Without a lasting power of attorney, the guardianship court appoints a legal guardian, even for spouses.

schritte.titel: Bank power of attorney beyond death
schritte.text: It is granted in addition on the form of every bank at which a securities account is held. In practice, a general power of attorney on its own is often not accepted immediately.

It is either written entirely by hand with date and signature or drawn up by a notary. The notarial will later replaces the certificate of inheritance and makes securities accounts available more quickly.

A list of all securities accounts, bank accounts, insurance policies, building savings contracts and access details, kept separately from the passwords and checked every year. Without such a list, heirs spend months searching for holdings they know nothing about.

bloecke.md: Banks notify the inheritance tax office of a deceased person's balances and securities holdings (Section 33 ErbStG). Only for small amounts may the notification be omitted under the Inheritance Tax Implementing Ordinance (Erbschaftsteuer-Durchführungsverordnung). The recipient must notify the acquisition themselves within three months of learning of it (Section 30 ErbStG). This also applies to gifts, and even if the acquisition will certainly remain below the allowance. For notarised transactions, the notary reports it. The tax office then requests the tax return separately (Section 31 ErbStG).

bloecke.titel: Compulsory share (Pflichtteil) and the ten-year period
bloecke.md:
Children, spouses and in certain circumstances parents can be disinherited, but retain a monetary claim equal to half of their statutory share of the inheritance (Section 2303 BGB). Gifts made in the last ten years before death are included in the calculation under Section 2325 BGB, with their weight falling by one tenth each year. A gift made seven full years ago, for example, still counts at 30%. For gifts to a spouse, this period only begins when the marriage ends and therefore does not run out during the marriage.

The period under Section 14 ErbStG and that under Section 2325 BGB cover the same length of time but serve different purposes. A transfer that is optimal for tax purposes can trigger a compulsory share claim that exceeds the tax saved.

mitnehmen: The allowance applies per relationship and ten-year period, regardless of the number of transfers, and is then renewed in full. This staggering is the most effective planning option and only takes time.

Inheritance tax and flat-rate withholding tax successively burden the same assets, because the price on the date of death does not become new acquisition costs and Section 35b EStG does not apply to capital income.
The tax depends on the value on the valuation date. If the market falls after the date of death, the tax does not fall with it, and the money for it has to come from the remaining assets.
The exemption for an inherited family home requires ten years of owner occupation, and this commitment can be more expensive than the tax saved.
A lasting power of attorney and a power of attorney beyond death cost little and save the months in which nobody could otherwise get at the securities account.

begriffe.text: Inheritance and gift tax are based on the values on the day the tax arises (Section 11 ErbStG), that is, on the date of death in the case of inheritance. Later price changes are disregarded.

Rule in Section 19(3) ErbStG under which, when a value threshold is exceeded, at most half of the excess above the threshold may be additionally taxed, and at most three quarters for tax rates above 30%.
Right to use an item and draw its income without being its owner (Section 1030 BGB). Its capitalised value under Section 14 BewG reduces the value of a gift for tax purposes.

begriffe.begriff: Power of attorney beyond death (Vollmacht über den Tod hinaus)
begriffe.text: Bank power of attorney that does not expire on death. It gives the authorised person access to the account and securities account before the heirs' status has been proven.
Several heirs form a joint ownership community (Gesamthandsgemeinschaft, Sections 2032 et seq. BGB). They can only dispose of individual estate assets jointly (Section 2040 BGB).

Owner-occupied residential property that passes tax-free under Section 13(1) nos. 4a to 4c ErbStG. For acquisitions upon death, the exemption for spouses and children is tied to ten years of owner occupation, and for children it is additionally limited to 200 square metres of living space.
